project.title: Quantum Error Correction Using Neural Graph States
project.research_question: Can graph neural networks improve decoder threshold efficiency under correlated depolarizing noise?
objectives: Benchmark GNN-based decoders against minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM).
Evaluate syndrome extraction latency across code distances 3, 5, and 7.
project.claimed_contribution: A real-time neural decoding architecture achieving 1.8% threshold under circuit-level noise.
project.methodology: We simulate toric and surface codes using Stim, train message passing neural networks on syndrome hypergraphs, and benchmark decoding throughput on GPU accelerators.
project.dataset_or_materials: Synthetic syndrome measurement dataset consisting of 100,000 Monte Carlo error trajectories generated at error rates p=0.001 to 0.02.
project.results: The neural decoder improves logical error rates by 23% over MWPM at distance 5 while reducing decoding runtime from 4.2ms to 0.8ms per measurement round.
project.limitations: Training overhead scales with code distance, and decoding accuracy degrades slightly under asymmetric drift noise.

source_draft: Quantum computers require active error correction to protect qubits against decoherence. Conventional decoders like MWPM and union-find are scalable but suboptimal for correlated multi-qubit noise. We train an equivariant graph neural network directly on topological syndrome graphs. Our results show substantial latency improvements and lower logical failure probabilities across varied physical error rates.

references.text: Fowler, A. G., et al. (2012). Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation. Physical Review A, 86(3), 032324.
Dennis, E., et al. (2002). Topological quantum memory. Journal of Mathematical Physics, 43(9), 4452-4505.
